nodes.title: Register the component as the control's accessor

anchor.snippet: { provide: NG_VALUE_ACCESSOR, useExisting: forwardRef(() => QuantityStepperComponent), multi: true }

nodes.why: formControlName looks for NG_VALUE_ACCESSOR on its element; useExisting hands the form this instance, and forwardRef covers the class being declared after its decorator.
nodes.alternative: Inject NgControl into the component and set ngControl.valueAccessor = this.
nodes.tradeoff: The provider works with every form directive and is the documented pattern; injecting NgControl also exposes the control's validity but needs care to avoid a circular provider.

nodes.title: Keep the shown value in a signal
nodes.why: The form writes the value from outside the template, through writeValue; a signal write is what marks this OnPush view for check when that happens.
nodes.alternative: A plain value field that writeValue assigns.
nodes.tradeoff: A plain field can look right on the first render, but after form.reset() the OnPush stepper keeps the old number, because nothing in the parent changes its inputs.

nodes.title: Derive each button from value, flag and bound

anchor.snippet: protected readonly canIncrease = computed(() => !this.disabled() && this.value() < this.max());

nodes.why: The + button depends on the disabled flag, the value and the max input; a computed recalculates it when any of the three changes, and the template only binds the result.
nodes.alternative: Write the full condition in each disabled binding of the template.
nodes.tradeoff: Inline conditions are shorter to read once, but the rule would then live in two places, and step() could drift from what the buttons allow.

nodes.title: Accept what the form writes, null included
nodes.why: writeValue runs on start, setValue, patchValue and reset; a nullable form resets to null, which falls back to the minimum instead of rendering an empty stepper.
nodes.alternative: Ignore null and keep the previous value on screen.
nodes.tradeoff: Falling back to min shows a number the form does not hold until the next change; keeping the old value would show a number the form already discarded.

nodes.title: Report a change only when the value moved
nodes.why: The form hears about user changes only through the callback it registered; step() calls it after clamping, and the early return keeps a click at a bound from marking the control dirty.
nodes.alternative: Call the change callback on every click, or from writeValue as well.
nodes.tradeoff: Calling it from writeValue would echo every form write back as a user edit; skipping no-op clicks costs one comparison.

nodes.title: Report a touch when focus leaves
nodes.why: The (focusout) host listener calls markTouched(), which forwards to the registered callback, so the control becomes touched the way a native input does on blur.
nodes.alternative: Mark the control touched on the first click instead.
nodes.tradeoff: Touched on click flags the control earlier, which suits steppers used only by mouse; focusout matches the built-in accessors and keyboard users.
